title: Alternating maps extend uniquely through module sheafification
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small relative to the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let $A$ be a presheaf of commutative rings, and let $P$ be a presheaf of $A$-modules: each $P(V)$ is an $A(V)$-module and restrictions are semilinear over restrictions of $A$. Let $A^\#$ and $P^\#$ be their sheafifications [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], with the induced $A^\#$-module structure on $P^\#$. For $n\geq0$ define $\bigwedge^n_{A^\#}P^\#$ as the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigwedge^n_{A^\#(V)}P^\#(V)$, using [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $F$ be any sheaf of $A^\#$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Evaluation on wedges of images of sections of $P$ induces a bijection
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{A^\#}\left(\bigwedge^n_{A^\#}P^\#,F\right)\cong\left\{(b_V)_V: b_V:P(V)^n\to F(V)\text{ is }A(V)\text{-multilinear and alternating, and commutes with every restriction}\right\}.$$
Here $F(V)$ is viewed as an $A(V)$-module through $A(V)\to A^\#(V)$, alternating means zero whenever two entries are equal, and for $n=0$ the right side means a restriction-compatible family of elements of $F(V)$. The bijection sends $h$ to $b_V(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=h_V(\eta x_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\eta x_n)$, where $\eta:P\to P^\#$ is the sheafification map. It is natural in $F$ and in morphisms of $A$-module presheaves $P$.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules): finite-variable alternating extension of the module sheafification universal property, extracted as a separate statement; the single-variable assertion alone is not being used as this theorem.

proof.text: Write $B=A^\#$, $Q=P^\#$, and let $u:A\to B$ and $\eta:P\to Q$ be the units. The module-sheafification interface gives the $B$-action on $Q$, compatible with the $A$-action on $P$, and identifies the underlying abelian sheaf with abelian sheafification. Forgetting abelian groups and commutative rings to sets therefore identifies $|\eta|$ and $|u|$ with set-sheafification units. Since set-sheafification preserves finite limits, for every finite $k$ the map $|P|^k\to |Q|^k$ is a set-sheafification unit. The same holds for $|A|\times |P|^k\to |B|\times |Q|^k$. For $k=0$ this includes the final presheaf and final sheaf. Consequently maps from any of these sheafified products to $|F|$ are determined uniquely by their composites with the indicated units.

source.place: Tags 00WJ (lemma-sheafification-exact), 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), and section-sheaves-algebraic-structures; module action: 03CY in sites-modules.tex

proof.text: A family $b$ on the right side of the statement is a morphism of presheaves of sets $|P|^n\to |F|$. Apply the product sheafification of step 1 and the sheafification universal property to obtain a unique morphism of sheaves of sets $c:|Q|^n\to |F|$ with $c\eta^n=b$. In particular $c$ commutes with restriction along every site morphism. This assertion for $n=0$ extends the given map from the final presheaf to $|F|$ to the final sheaf.

source.place: Tag 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint), applied to the finite products furnished by Tag 00WJ

proof.text: For each slot $i$, compare the maps $|Q|^{n+1}\to |F|$ given by $c(\ldots,x_i+y_i,\ldots)$ and $c(\ldots,x_i,\ldots)+c(\ldots,y_i,\ldots)$. Their composites with $|P|^{n+1}$ agree by additivity of $b$, so step 1 makes them equal. Compare likewise the maps $|B|\times |Q|^n\to |F|$ given by $c(\ldots,a x_i,\ldots)$ and $a\,c(\ldots,x_i,\ldots)$: on $|A|\times |P|^n$ they agree by $A$-linearity of $b$ and compatibility of the units with actions, hence agree everywhere. Finally, for $i\ne j$, insert the same variable in slots $i,j$ to compare $c\circ\delta_{ij}:|Q|^{n-1}\to |F|$ with zero. On $|P|^{n-1}$ both are zero by alternation of $b$; step 1 again proves equality. Thus $c_V$ is $B(V)$-multilinear and alternating. The first two comparisons require $n\geq1$ and the last requires $n\geq2$; for $n=0$ all conditions are vacuous.

source.place: Tags 00WH and 00WJ: equality by the universal property on finite products; action compatibility from sites-modules.tex, Tag 03CY

proof.text: Let $W(V)=\bigwedge^n_{B(V)}Q(V)$, with the semilinear restrictions induced by those of $B$ and $Q$. The ordinary exterior-power universal property gives a unique $B(V)$-linear map $t_V:W(V)\to F(V)$ satisfying $t_V(q_1\wedge\cdots\wedge q_n)=c_V(q_1,\ldots,q_n)$. These maps commute with restrictions: for an arrow $f:V'\to V$, the two composites $W(V)\to F(V')$ are $B(V)$-linear when the target action is restricted along $B(f)$. On every wedge they have values $F(f)c_V(q_1,\ldots,q_n)$ and $c_{V'}(Q(f)q_1,\ldots,Q(f)q_n)$, equal because $c$ is a sheaf map. They therefore agree by the uniqueness part of that same universal property. Hence $t:W\to F$ is a morphism of presheaves of $B$-modules.

source.place: Tag 00DM (section-tensor-algebra), alternating quotient and wedge generators; exact universal property in the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: Apply module sheafification with coefficient presheaf already the sheaf $B$. The presheaf map $t$ factors uniquely as $W\to W^\#\xrightarrow{h}F$, with $h$ a $B$-module-sheaf morphism. By the definition in the statement $W^\#=\bigwedge_B^n Q$, and its formula on wedges of images from $P$ is precisely $h_V(\eta x_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\eta x_n)=b_V(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$. Conversely every $h$ yields such a family by composing its underlying map with the wedge map and $\eta^n$, which are restriction-compatible and alternating multilinear. If two $h$ give the same family, their wedge evaluations $|Q|^n\to |F|$ agree by step 1. Their induced linear maps $W(V)\to F(V)$ then agree by exterior-power uniqueness, and the two sheaf maps agree by module-sheafification uniqueness. This proves that the constructions are inverse bijections.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules) with the coefficient presheaf already a sheaf; exterior universal property: algebra.tex, Tag 00DM

proof.text: For a module-sheaf morphism $v:F\to F'$, wedge evaluation of $v\circ h$ is $(v_V\circ b_V)_V$. For a morphism of $A$-module presheaves $g:P'\to P$, its sheafification satisfies $g^\#\eta'=\eta g$; hence evaluation of $h\circ\bigwedge^n g^\#$ at $(x_i)$ is $b_V(g_Vx_1,\ldots,g_Vx_n)$. The exterior map here sends a pure wedge to the wedge of its images, as follows directly from the alternating quotient defining the exterior algebra. Uniqueness already proved makes these the naturality squares. For $n=0$, $W(V)=B(V)$ and $t_V(a)=a\,c_V(*)$; the empty wedge is $1$, and evaluation gives the original compatible family of elements of $F(V)$. No choice of sections or local lifts enters these formulas.

My own proof: Hom(W#,F) = Hom_B-presheaf(W,F), which equals the alternating multilinear set-sheaf maps |Q|^n->|F|, which by density along |P|^n->|Q|^n equals the family b. Step 1 gives finite-product sheafification units, using that A is commutative and the site small. Step 3 transfers additivity, scalars via u(a)eta(x)=eta(ax), and alternation (vanishing on the diagonal, valid with 2-torsion) by uniqueness. Step 4: naturality as B(V)-linear maps into the restricted F(V'), correct. Step 5: injectivity goes through step 1, then exterior uniqueness, then sheafification uniqueness, never assuming surjectivity of the unit. Small cases n=0, n=1, n=2 with 2F=0, P=0 and the zero ring all check out. No new nodes; proof_deps equals the union of uses; no SGA.
